question: Who among the following rulers inscribed his messages to his subjects and officials on stone surfaces?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashoka**__ was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty.
 
• Ashoka was also known as **Devanam Priyadasi.**
 
• Ashoka invaded Kalinga in 261 B.C, In** Kalinga War.**
 
• __**He inscribed his messages to his subjects and officials on stone surfaces.**__
 
• Ashoka was the first king in Indian history who has left his records engraved on stones.
 
• Many edicts were built by Ashoka throughout India, including in modern-day** Nepal and Pakistan.**
 
• **Pataliputra (Patna) **was his capital, and Taxila and Ujjain were his regional capitals.
 
• Ashoka personally led the battle against the Kalingas in 265 BC, and he was successful in defeating the Kalingas.
 __
 
• He was so shocked by the horrors of war that he determined to abstain from violence for the rest of his life and devote himself to Buddhism.
 
• Ashoka converted to Buddhism around **263 BC. **
 
• A Buddhist monk named **Moggaliputta Tissa** became his mentor.
 
• In 250 BC, under the chair of **Moggaliputta Tissa**, Ashoka convened the** third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** was the founder of the Maurya Empire in ancient India who ruled between 321–297 BCE.
 
• **Bindusara** was the second Mauryan emperor of India who ruled between 297- 273 BCE.
 
• **Chandragupta I** was the first emperor of the Gupta dynasty.
